newsitem.title: USA: Kazakhstan promotes Eurobond, US analysts lukewarm.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan promotes Eurobond, US analysts lukewarm.

text.p: Kazakhstan promoted its inaugural Eurobond issue on Thursday, but market sources said the issue scheduled to launch next week may get a low-key reception compared to the fanfare surrounding Russia's global bond issue in November.
ABN-Amro Hoare Govett, the lead manager, said the three-year issue would be offered only to qualified insitutional buyers under Section 144-A of U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission regulations.
Kazakhstan received a Ba3 rating from Moody's and BB minus from Standard & Poor's.
"We think 9-3/4 to 10 percent is likely" said a portfolio manager, predicting an issue of $100 million to $200 million.
Kazakh Prime miniter Akezhan Kazhegeldin said earlier that he expected the yield would be 9.75 to 10 percent.

Although Kazakhstan stacks up favorbly against other similarly rated countries in terms of external debt and endowment in natural resources, there were concerns about the country's tax collection, wage arrears and various projects to transport Kazakh oil and gas to the world market, he said."
Grigory Marchenko, chairman of the National Security Committee, told investors that the country did not need the funds but it wanted to establish a track record.
"We do it for the sake of putting our name on the map," he said.

Kazakhstan secured pledge of over $1.2 billion in aid from various donor countries and multinational groups. In addition, it can draw from $450 million from a three-year program beginning 1996, he said.
Marchenko said Kazakhstan may issue samurai bonds next year, but no decision had been made.
